images.title: Constructions and tilings
images.purpose: Recap the two big ideas of the chapter in one frame: equal arcs give constructions, and tiling covers a region with no gaps and no overlaps.
images.composition: Two equal halves: on the left one finished perpendicular bisector construction, on the right one small tiled grid, each with a one line caption and wide white space.
exact_structure: Left half: a dark horizontal segment XY with endpoints labelled X and Y.
Two grey (#6B7280) arcs of the same radius, one centred at X and one centred at Y, each long enough to cross the other once above and once below the segment (2 crossing points).
A reddish purple (#CC79A7) line through the two crossing points, cutting XY at its midpoint, with a small square right angle mark; caption below: equal arcs.

Right half: a grid of 2 rows and 4 columns covered by exactly 4 horizontal 2 × 1 tiles, two in the top row filled teal (#0072B2) and two in the bottom row filled amber (#E69F00), all with thick dark outlines; caption below: no gaps, no overlaps.
rejection: the reddish purple line not passing through both arc crossings or not perpendicular to XY
the grid with other than 2 rows and 4 columns or other than 4 tiles
a protractor or any degree label drawn
images.takeaway: Equal arcs and congruent triangles give every construction in the chapter, and tiling means covering a region with no gaps and no overlaps.
images.description: On the left, the perpendicular bisector of XY drawn with grey arcs and a reddish purple line; on the right, a 2 by 4 grid covered by four 2 × 1 tiles.
images.context: Shown beside the chapter summary text and recap video.
images.teaching_notes: Use the left half to recall the construction ideas and the right half to recall what tiling means, then pose the two open questions.

image_decisions.why: One frame recaps the chapter's two big ideas, constructions from equal arcs and tiling.
